units.title: What does the NBLS Act govern, and what counts as land surveying?
units.examGoal: Recognize the professional statute and understand the statutory scope of the practice of land surveying and the Association.
recognitionCues: statute governing the practice of land surveying in New Brunswick
professional/Association regulation of a surveying body
mustRecall: locating things relative to boundaries can constitute practice;
watercourse boundary work and preparation of related plans/documents/advice fall within the statutory scope.

units.title: Who may practise, and how may firms practise?
units.examGoal: Distinguish individual registration from organizational authorization to practise.
coreUnderstanding: distinction between individual registration and organizational authorization;
mustRecall: Individual practice is tied to registration under the Act, while partnerships, associations and corporations practise through the Act’s organizational-authorization framework.

mustLocate.prompt: who may practise as a registered land surveyor

units.title: How are the ANBLS Bylaws organized and what do they add to the Act?

bylaw part-numbered structure (e.g. 2.1, 3.1, 6.5)
coreUnderstanding: the Bylaws operationalize the Association: membership, governance, practice standards and discipline details;
the Act sets out the statutory framework while the Bylaws govern internal Association life.

coreUnderstanding: boundary confirmation resolves disputes/uncertainties over land boundaries by a statutory decision process;
the confirmed boundary then carries legal effect.

units.title: What must accompany a boundary-confirmation application?
units.examGoal: Understand the application package for boundary confirmation and what the surveyor’s report addresses.
coreUnderstanding: the application package can involve: current survey; field notes; surveyor’s report; instruments; affected owners/interests; supporting evidence.
the surveyor’s report addresses: issue; boundary history; evidence; reasoning for accepting/rejecting competing boundary evidence.
mustRecall: A boundary-confirmation surveyor’s report addresses the issue to be determined, the history of the boundary, the evidence relied on, and the reasons for accepting or rejecting competing boundary evidence.

units.title: What is the Registry system and when does the Registry Act matter?
units.examGoal: Recognize the Registry system, understand when the Registry Act matters, and understand the distinction from Land Titles.
recognitionCues: deeds-based / registry system of land registration
registry office, registrar and registration of instruments
coreUnderstanding: the Registry is a deeds-based system: instruments are registered in order and affect priority;
distinct from the Land Titles system, where registration vests and insures title.

units.title: What is registration supposed to accomplish?
units.examGoal: Understand what registration accomplishes, using the legal effect of registration as the conceptual anchor.
coreUnderstanding: legal effect of registration: a duly registered conveyance transfers the land described according to the intent of the conveyance (s.34).
mustRecall: A duly registered conveyance has statutory effect to transfer the land described according to the intent of the conveyance (Registry Act s.34).

mustLocate.prompt: legal effect of a registered conveyance

units.title: What is the Land Titles system and how is it different from Registry?

registration under Land Titles insures registered ownership, unlike deeds-based Registry.
mustRecall: Land Titles registration is the primary evidence of registered ownership of the land.
